title: Vanilla JS
body:
Plain [[JavaScript]] and the browser's own [[Web APIs]], with no framework or library
underneath. The joke name for "no jQuery, no [[React]], just the language".

Everything in this course up to the [[MERN Stack]] is vanilla JS: `document.querySelector`,
`addEventListener`, `fetch`, `classList`. It is worth learning in that order because a
framework hides these rather than replacing them. [[React]] still produces DOM mutations in
the end; it just decides which ones for you, via a [[Virtual DOM]] diff.

The practical argument for vanilla is that it ships nothing: no download, no build step, no
version upgrade, no [[Module Bundler]]. The argument against is that anything stateful gets
written by hand, which is what [[Modifying Documents]] and [[Event Delegation]] look like once
a page has more than a couple of moving parts.
